title: Cygnus X-1 vs Sagittarius A* vs TON 618 | Black Hole Mass Comparison #shorts
description_hook: From a black hole of about 21 Suns to an estimated 60 billion: black holes, ranked by mass.

items.name: CYGNUS X-1
items.label: 21 SUNS
items.say: How heavy can a black hole get? Start with Cygnus X-1, the first one ever identified. About 21 times the mass of the Sun.
items.img: a small black hole pulling a glowing stream of gas off a bright blue companion star, swirling orange accretion disk, deep starfield

items.name: GAIA BH3
items.label: 33 SUNS
items.say: Gaia BH3, the heaviest known stellar black hole in our galaxy: 33 Suns.
items.img: a quiet dark black hole bending the light of a yellow star orbiting it, faint lensing ring, sparse starry background

items.name: SAGITTARIUS A*
items.label: 4.3 MILLION SUNS
items.say: Sagittarius A Star, at the center of the Milky Way. About 4.3 million Suns.
items.img: the dense glowing core of a spiral galaxy with a dark shadow at its heart, crowded golden stars and dust lanes swirling around it

items.name: M87*
items.label: 5.4 BILLION SUNS
items.say: M87 Star, the first black hole ever photographed. 5.4 billion Suns.
items.img: a blurry glowing orange ring of light around a perfectly dark center, soft and hazy, floating in black space

items.name: TON 618
items.label: 60+ BILLION SUNS
items.say: TON 618. Estimated at more than 60 billion Suns.
items.img: a blinding quasar at the edge of the universe, an immense bright core with twin jets of light shooting into darkness

items.name: EARTH AS A BLACK HOLE
items.say: Now crush Earth into a black hole. All of it, squeezed to a radius of 9 millimeters: a ball 2 centimeters across.
items.img: a tiny dark marble-sized sphere floating in front of a distant blue planet glow, warped starlight bending around it

gumi.say: Gumi's verdict: your whole planet would fit in your fist. Sleep well.
